reasoning: A wins. Both attempts do the same thing on the server: they track blocks in a table keyed by part, check ownership by UserId, share the rate-limit and reach checks, and clear the occupied cell. Their client input handling is also nearly the same. B adds a useful `Destroying` cleanup and a client-side owner pre-filter, but it fails StyLua on its own lines. A is equally correct, passes every check, and is ready to merge as it is.

criteria.note: Removal is added to BlockPlacement.server.luau and BlockPlacer.luau using the same patterns, with small helpers (`isRateLimited`, `isInReach`, `waitForRemote`), and no new framework or layout.
The server-side table `placedBlocks[part] = {Cell, OwnerUserId}` is checked against `player.UserId`, and nothing the client sends is trusted.

`typeof(block) ~= "Instance"` plus the server's own table lookup reject any foreign instance; the shared `isRateLimited` and `isInReach(player, placed.Cell)` checks run, then `occupied[placed.Cell] = nil` frees the cell.

A right-click counts only if it is quick and still (at most 0.3 s and 5 px), so dragging to turn the camera doesn't remove; TouchLongPress removes on Begin with one touch; both paths check gameProcessed; click and tap to place are unchanged.
Only the two placement files change, placement still works, and luau-lsp, selene, and StyLua all pass.
Changes stay in the two existing files in their style; it adds a `getRootPart` helper and an `OwnerUserId` attribute.
The server-side `blocks[part]` record is checked against `player.UserId`; the attribute is only a client-side pre-filter.
Instance type check, record lookup, rate limit, and reach from `record.Cell` all run, and the cell is cleared; a `Destroying` handler also frees cells however a block goes away.
Right-click and long-press logic is sound and the press is gated on gameProcessed in InputBegan, but `onInputEnded` doesn't look at gameProcessed itself.
The logic is correct, but StyLua fails on the long `rightClickStart = {...}` line, and the `onTouchLongPress` signature is reformatted too.

strengths: Clean server-side ownership table keyed by part
Rate limit and reach checks are shared helpers used by both place and remove
Handles right-click versus camera drag sensibly
weaknesses: If a block is destroyed by something other than RemoveBlock, its cell stays marked as occupied
The client doesn't filter out other players' blocks before firing (harmless, since the server refuses them)

strengths: `Destroying` hook keeps `occupied` consistent however a block is removed
Client pre-filters by the owner attribute, which saves wasted remote calls
weaknesses: Fails stylua --check in its own code
Adds an attribute as well as the server table, which is slightly redundant
